messages.author: 83cfdad7795d551d
messages.subject: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
I just started using the package "blavaan". However, when I try to
compare two different models, I get the following error:

blavCompare(fitLearn_bcfa_free,fitLearn_bcfa_constr)
Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds

Could you please explain to me what this might mean?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
Davide,

I'm not sure that I've seen this error before. First check to ensure you have the latest versions of lavaan and blavaan via, e.g.,

install.packages("lavaan")
install.packages("blavaan")

If that doesn't work, it would help to see your model and data.

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
If you haven't, you might also check that you have the newest version of lavaan (separately from blavaan).

But, in your case, I think the test="none" argument is the culprit. blavCompare() will not work with this argument (and I should add a check for this).

You might also consider using the scale() function on more observed variables, because I also see a warning about observed variances being very different from each another.

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
Davide,

As we discussed off-list, the error appears to go away when incomplete cases are removed. In the "incomplete data" case, I believe the issue is related to this:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/lavaan/00SVZOOwclk/Fixgg03WPmwJ;context-place=forum/lavaan


Looking at your model some more, there might also be problems stemming from the latent variable "Intercept" because there is only one observed variable corresponding to it. Instead, the observed variable "int" could have a regression relationship with other lvs. You might try something like this

model_Learn_cfa_free <- '
# latent variables
OS =~ score_OS + score_SS
PET =~ math + hebrew
Gf =~ ETS_V + ETS_Loc
CRT_arb=~ crt_112 + crt_212
CRT_narb=~ crt_111 + crt_211
int ~ OS + PET + Gf + CRT_arb + CRT_narb
'

fitLearn_bcfa_free <- bcfa(model_Learn_cfa_free, data=mc)


And then the constrained model could just have int ~ 1 instead of the last line.

Ed
